_about: Tables for science/SCIENTIFIC_EQUIPMENT.md: the capability model and a seed catalogue of scientific apparatus from antiquity to now. Rex (2026-10-29): research all chemistry equipment from then until now, with dates and fuel and power requirements, so the world can be configured and a time-anomaly piece plugged in without rebuilding. The seed is the keeper's; completing it is a belt research task. Dates are the usual attributions and vary by source; period availability is for 1650 to 1730 in the Atlantic. mark: rex | proposed | open. Tables moved whole to data/library/equipment.json (no game columns): roles, assembly, confidence.

catalogue.title: The equipment catalogue (researched and reconciled 2026-10-29; from antiquity to now; expandable, 300 is not a maximum)
catalogue.source: Usual attributions (Wikipedia timelines of microscope technology and element discovery, Museo Galileo on the air pump, encyclopaedia entries on the barometer, histories of chemistry and alchemical apparatus; EQ-*). Dates vary by source and are the common ones; capabilities are the keeper's estimates from the apparatus's physics (a charcoal fire with bellows reaches about 1,200 C; a sand bath 300; a water bath 100) and are placeholders until researched per item. Period availability: 1650 to 1730, Atlantic.

wear.title: Wear and calibration: condition as three independent properties (proposed; ties the science system to the ship's maintenance loop)
wear.source: ChatGPT's suggestion (outside AI), recorded: a poorly kept balance drifts, a damaged furnace will not hold heat. Rex's maintenance design is PIRATE.md 5a and DUTIES.md (keeps / if skipped); this table is the same shape for apparatus, so the economy's facilities and the laboratory age like the ship. Refined 2026-10-29 (ChatGPT, outside AI, agreed): condition is not one number; a damaged furnace may still reach its maximum and fail to hold it, a worn seal lowers pressure and not heat, a drifted thermometer misreports while the reaction proceeds normally.
